s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with pleuritic and intermittent characteristics, associated with diaphoresis and elevated troponin levels, in a young adult with recent onset of inflammatory bowel disease
salient_findings: Pleuritic pain worsened by sitting forward
Extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
key_facts: 2-day history of intermittent, sharp, central chest pain
Diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 3 weeks prior
No family history of cardiovascular disease
ECG shows sinus rhythm with benign early repolarization
Negative serum viral and autoantibody screens

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Pleuritic chest pain, elevated troponin, and inflammatory markers suggest myocardial and pericardial involvement

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin levels and chest pain are consistent with acute coronary syndrome, despite the patient's young age

shortlist.label: Inflammatory bowel disease-associated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Recent diagnosis of ulcerative colitis and cardiac symptoms suggest a possible link between the two conditions

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, inflammatory markers, and cardiac symptoms are consistent with myocarditis, which can be caused by various factors including autoimmune diseases

shortlist.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous disease such as sarcoidosis can cause cardiac symptoms and elevated inflammatory markers, and the patient's recent diagnosis of ulcerative colitis increases the suspicion for an autoimmune etiology

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of sharp, central chest pain, elevated high-sensitivity troponin T, and extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) are consistent with myocarditis. The CMR findings, including mild systolic dysfunction and hypokinesia of the anterolateral and inferolateral segments, further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: The absence of pericardial effusion on transthoracic echocardiography and CMR makes myopericarditis less likely.

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's young age, lack of family history of cardiovascular disease, and absence of significant coronary artery disease risk factors make acute coronary syndrome less likely.

rejected.label: Inflammatory bowel disease-associated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has ulcerative colitis, the temporal relationship between the diagnosis and the cardiac symptoms, as well as the lack of other supporting evidence, makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The absence of other supporting evidence, such as lung involvement or lymphadenopathy, and the lack of granulomas on imaging make cardiac sarcoidosis less likely.
